question: As of March 2025, under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM) how many supercomputers have been deployed across India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Supercomputing Mission (NSM)** was launched by the Government of India to enhance the country’s supercomputing capacity and capability in research and development.
 
• As of **March 2025**, a total of **34 supercomputers** have been deployed across India under the NSM initiative.
 
• The supercomputers have been installed in various **educational and research institutions** to foster innovation in areas such as weather forecasting, computational biology, artificial intelligence, and material science.
 
• NSM is a collaboration between the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** and the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, with the systems built indigenously by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC).
 
• The mission aims to establish a network of supercomputers with a combined computational capacity of over **64 Petaflops**, greatly enhancing India's computational infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Supercomputing Mission (NSM):**

 
 
• The mission was launched in **2015** with an outlay of **Rs. 4,500 crore**.
 
• It focuses on developing an **indigenous supercomputing ecosystem** to reduce reliance on imported technology.
 
• NSM is being implemented in **three phases**, with the final phase targeting the development of systems with exascale computing capabilities.
 
• The mission emphasizes the use of **Make in India** components, with efforts to produce over 60% of the hardware domestically.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Supercomputing in India:**
 
 
• Supercomputers are used in **weather prediction** to forecast cyclones, monsoons, and other climate-related events.
 
• They assist in **drug discovery** and molecular modeling, especially during pandemics like COVID-19.
 
• Supercomputing is crucial for **simulations in astrophysics**, material science, and particle physics experiments.
 
• It supports **artificial intelligence (AI)** and machine learning (ML) applications in fields like defense, healthcare, and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Deployed Supercomputers:**
 
 
• **Param Siddhi-AI:** A high-performance AI supercomputer ranked among the top 100 globally (as of 2023).
 
• **Param Shivay:** Installed at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, it was the first system deployed under NSM.
 
• **Param Brahma:** Deployed at IISER Pune, it aids in advanced scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India’s supercomputing initiative places it among countries like the **USA, China, and Japan**, which are pioneers in high-performance computing.
 
• The global leader in supercomputing as of 2023 is the **Fugaku** supercomputer from Japan, which has a peak performance of over 442 Petaflops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of C-DAC:** The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) plays a pivotal role in designing and deploying supercomputers under NSM.
 
• **Petaflop Computing:** The term "Petaflop" refers to a computer's ability to perform one quadrillion floating-point operations per second, a critical measure of speed for high-performance computing.
 
• **Indigenous Efforts:** Developing supercomputers locally helps reduce dependence on foreign technology and enhances India’s technological sovereignty.
 
• **Future Goals:** India aims to build systems capable of **exascale computing**, which would perform a billion billion calculations per second.
